raw_response:
My family has farmed this land in Quzhou for generations. My father grew wheat and corn, his father grew wheat and corn, and that's what I'll grow too. I know these crops. I know when the ground feels right to plant, when the leaves look wrong, when the water is low. I don't read the extension pamphlets but I talk to my neighbors at the village store and I watch what works.

In Quzhou we always do winter wheat first, then summer corn on the same land. That's just how it's done here. The wheat goes in around the Cold Dew festival, comes out in June, then I turn around and put corn in right away before the summer rains get going.

I have about 8 mu of fields. I'll plant all of it in wheat this winter, then all of it in corn after the wheat comes off.

For seeds, I buy whatever the village seed shop has. They sell hybrid corn — everyone does it now, been that way for years — so I'll get that. For wheat I usually keep some from last year's grain or buy the local improved variety, whatever my neighbor Zhang uses.

Fertilizer, I put down a good amount. My father always said more is better. I'll put the fertilizer in before planting and again when it's growing. I've seen plots that didn't get enough and the plants look thin and pale. I don't want that.

Irrigation: our county depends on groundwater. For wheat I'll water it in before winter, again in spring when it joints, and once more when it heads. Corn I water less — the summer rains usually help — but if it gets dry in August I'll run the pump.

I spray for weeds after planting and again if I see bugs or blight. Two or three times for wheat, once or twice for corn.
